transcript.text: t/d keeps cutting out after 10 mins then starts again if i leave it. vent hose goes out the window. pls help

That pattern most often means the dryer is overheating: its safety cut-out stops it, then it works again once it has cooled. With a vented dryer, a fluff-filled filter or restricted hose is the usual reason. A weak thermostat/thermal cut-out is possible, but only after airflow is proved clear. 1. Switch off and unplug it. Remove and clean the lint/fluff filter thoroughly. Clear any visible fluff around its housing. A heavily clogged filter supports overheating as the cause.
2. Check the hose from the dryer to the window: it should be as short and straight as practical, with no kinks, crushing, water in low loops, or fluff blockage. Check the outlet is not pressed against a closed window or blocked by a grille. Poor airflow points to the same overheating cause.
3. Avoid overloading it for the next test; use a normal-sized load. An overloaded drum can restrict airflow through laundry. If the filter and hose are cleaned/clear but it still cuts out after roughly 10 minutes, the blower fan or the thermostat/thermal cut-out needs checking by an appliance engineer. Do not keep running it if there is a burning smell, smoke, or scorching: unplug it and stop using it.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
ok did the filter, its clean. hose is crushed behind the dryer tho i pushed it back recently, has fluff in the folds. cabinet gets really hot before it stops, no burning smell

The crushed hose with fluff trapped in its folds is very likely the cause. It is restricting the hot air leaving the dryer, so the cabinet gets excessively hot and the overheat cut-out stops it; it resets once cooled. 1. Switch off and unplug the dryer. Pull it forward carefully and remove the vent hose.
2. Clear all fluff from the hose and make sure it is not split, flattened or permanently kinked. If it will not spring back to a round, open shape, replace the hose rather than trying to use it crushed.
3. Refit it as short and straight as practical, with no tight bends or low loops. Make sure the window end is open to the outside and not pinched shut.
4. Only then try a normal-sized load while staying nearby. If it still cuts out after the hose has a clear, unrestricted air path, stop using it and arrange an engineer: the blower fan or thermostat/thermal cut-out would then be the likely fault. Do not run it again if it becomes extremely hot, smells of burning, smokes, or shows scorching.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
ok will pull it out and clear the fluff. if the hose is bent flat do i need a new one? its my landlords dryer btw

Yes — if it stays bent flat, crushed, split, or will not return to a properly round open tube after you remove it, it needs replacing. A flattened section still restricts airflow even if the fluff is cleared, and is a very plausible reason for the overheating and stopping. As it is your landlord’s dryer, I’d report the crushed, fluff-filled hose and the overheating/cut-out to them or the letting agent rather than paying for a repair yourself. Take a photo of the flattened hose if useful. After it is cleared, the useful distinction is:
1. If the hose opens up fully and can be routed without being trapped behind the dryer, it may be usable. Keep it short, with gentle bends only.
2. If it remains flattened or kinks as soon as the dryer is pushed back, replace the hose or alter the dryer position so it cannot be crushed.
3. That needs the landlord’s appliance engineer rather than further owner dismantling. Do not run it while the hose is crushed or if the cabinet again becomes excessively hot.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
